text: The Communist League (Danish: Kommunistisk Forbund; KF) was a political party in Denmark, founded on 21 January 1973 in Århus by the "Leninist Fraction," a group that had split from the Left Socialists (VS) in 1970 due to disillusionment over a lack of focus on labour struggles. The faction succeeded in adopting a new party programme and gained leadership of VS at its fourth congress in 1971, but internal conflicts intensified, peaking at the fifth congress in November 1972, after which the faction left VS despite securing a majority of delegates. They formed KF, with around 300 members following them, leaving VS with approximately 300 members. KF was primarily centered in Aarhus and Aalborg, the former being home to student activists in the 'Students Front,' while its Copenhagen branch remained weak. The party established new branches in Odense and Helsingør and became the leading force in the revolutionary left in those regions. KF launched the publications Vejen til Socialismen in 1976 and Arbejderpolitik in 1977. In 1975, factional conflicts arose within KF, with a group in Aarhus known as the "Coffee Club" (Kaffeklubben) proposing strategic changes; a document based on their inputs was approved ahead of the 1977 congress. In 1977, about 6% of delegates from Copenhagen formed the splinter group Kommunistisk Forbund - politik (KF-p), which adhered more closely to Leninism and argued that the 1917 October Revolution was the foundation of communist revolution in Denmark; after leaving KF, KF-p sought to join VS but were rejected due to political disagreements. The party was dissolved in 1980, with all members rejoining VS. During its existence, KF held seven congresses and organized various annual summer camps.
